title: Which README invariants fail?

evidence.I2: `get_invoice` authenticates but does not enforce tenant ownership on the fetched row; it calls `invoice_repo.get_by_id`, which performs a raw `db.get` by id with no tenant filter.
evidence.I3: Webhook idempotency is not robust: duplicate detection is only by `webhook_id`, and `_mark_processed` is written after side effects (`payments` write, `OrderPaid` outbox insert, and order status update). A retry/crash window can produce duplicate `OrderPaid` effects.
evidence.I4: Order status changes are not always cache-invalidating: `cancel_order` invalidates cache, but `mark_paid` changes status via `order_repo.update_status` without invalidating the order cache.

title: Review: list_orders performance smell

findings.summary: `get_order` returns cached rows before checking tenant ownership, and cache keys are only `order:{order_id}`. Because `list_orders` re-reads each row through `get_order`, a stale/wrong-tenant cached entry for the same order id can be returned to the current tenant.
`list_orders` first loads all tenant rows via `list_by_tenant`, then calls `get_order` per row, causing one extra repo/cache lookup per order (N+1 pattern) and redundant work.

title: Review: cache vs status change (I4)

findings.summary: `mark_paid` changes order status via `order_repo.update_status(order_id, "paid")` but never calls cache invalidation (`cache.invalidate_order`), so it does not satisfy README invariant I4 requiring invalidation on status change.
`cancel_order` explicitly invalidates cache after status change, which highlights the missing equivalent step in `mark_paid`.

title: Incident: duplicate OrderPaid

answer.root_cause: `handle_payment_webhook` does a non-atomic check-then-act: it inserts `OrderPaid` into outbox before recording `webhook_id` in `processed_webhooks`. If a retry-triggering error happens after outbox insert (e.g., during `order_service.mark_paid`), the webhook is not marked processed, so provider retries reinsert `OrderPaid` for the same `webhook_id`.

title: Incident: lost outbox events

answer.root_cause: In `process_once`, each row is acknowledged before it is published. If the worker crashes after `ack` but before `publish`, `claim_batch` will skip that row forever because it filters on `acked == False`, so the event disappears.

title: Constrained fix: webhook idempotency

plan_steps: In `service/payment_service.py`, add a helper that checks whether an `OrderPaid` outbox row already exists for the same tenant + payment (scan `outbox` rows, match `name == "OrderPaid"` and `payload.payment_id`).
In `handle_payment_webhook`, keep the webhook entrypoint unchanged, but gate `outbox.insert(order_paid(...))` behind that helper so retries do not enqueue a second `OrderPaid`.
Leave `_mark_processed(webhook_id)` at the end so successful full processing is still the completion signal; this avoids turning transient failures into permanently skipped processing.
answer.idempotency_change: Today the flow is: webhook_id duplicate check -> write payment -> unconditional `outbox.insert(OrderPaid)` -> mark order paid -> mark webhook processed. Change it to: webhook_id duplicate check -> write payment -> check whether `OrderPaid` for this payment already exists -> only insert if missing -> mark order paid -> mark webhook processed.
